items.title: A positive tilt matches the Poisson denominator

source.label: Zhou-Suzuki, Eq. (22)-(23)
source.anchor: Proposition B.7 proof A2.SS2.SSS2.p5, Eq22–23; standing n>=3,kappa>=4
source.attribution: Huanjian Zhou and Taiji Suzuki, On Complexity of Gaussian Sampling. Literal selected-parameter step in the proof of Proposition B.7. Omitted scalar algebra is supplied here; the Poisson integral and Eq24 remain separate.
source.scope: Only literal r/ell positivity and Eq22–23 denominator matching, including the coefficient equality; scalar identities hold for every real u, with no claim of positivity for every real u.

items.statement: Let natural \(n\ge3\) and real \(\kappa\ge4\), including \(\kappa=4\). Put \(s=\sqrt\kappa\), \(r=(1-1/n)(s-1)/(s+1)\), and \(\ell=(4ns+(s-1)^2)/(8n(n-1))\). Then \(0<r<1\), \(\ell>0\), and \(\ell=(\kappa-1)(1+r^2)/(8r)-(\kappa+1)/4\). Moreover \((\kappa-1)/(2r)=n(s+1)^2/(2(n-1))\). For every real \(u\), \(\kappa+1+4\ell-(\kappa-1)u=((\kappa-1)/(2r))(1+r^2-2ru)=(n(s+1)^2/(2(n-1)))(1+r^2-2ru)\). These are scalar identities; the source applies them to its actual \(U=O_{11}\).
assumptions: Every subtraction and division involving \(n\) is real arithmetic after coercion. The matching variable \(u\) is any real number. No domain estimate is supplied as a premise.

obligations.label: Literal Eq22 radius/tilt domains and Eq23 scalar denominator matching
